disease_label_per_paper: Chronic myelogenous leukemia with megakaryoblastic blast crisis and T315I mutation
presentation_summary: 42-year-old man initially presented with abdominal distension, fatigue, weakness, weight loss, mild pallor, and massive splenomegaly; initial CML was confirmed by BCR-ABL PCR.

After imatinib, hydroxyurea, dasatinib, and loss to follow-up, he returned one year later with rashes, upper abdominal and limb pain, general ill health, WBC 90 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 8 g/dL, platelets 19.10 x10^11/L, and 65% peripheral blasts.
Bone marrow had 80% blasts and CD61/CD34-positive megakaryoblastic features; T315I mutation was detected. He did not respond well to induction chemotherapy and died within a month.

risk_context.source_text_value: imatinib and hydroxyurea; no response to therapy; switched to dasatinib; lost to follow-up
Additional mutation analysis for imatinib resistance (T315I) by PCR was positive
